decision: PASS FOR DEEP DIVE / conditional implementation-planning lead, not implementation GO
scope_choice: Remove the authentic front door trim for access to a power-window motor, preserving real retaining clips, panel flex, inside-handle cage and rear connectors. Do not call this a completed motor repair.
proposed_instruction: Remove the front door trim for service and leave it supported without damaging the panel, clips, handle mechanism or wiring.
instruction_note: Ordinary procedural instructions are permitted by Version21; no invented event/order puzzle is needed. Final wording must match the selected actual assembly and start state.

exact_configuration.vehicle_target: Proposed donor: 2013 U.S. Hyundai Elantra UD 1.8L, left-front door and matching trim. Platform/service procedure is source-bound; a donor VIN/trim option, exact panel and clip part numbers, dimensions, mass and fitted connector variants still must be logged. Do not claim every 2013 vehicle uses one identical clip or switch pack.
exact_configuration.parts: Complete genuine matching door-side clip receptacles, trim panel and all its actual retaining clips; inside-handle cage with whatever original cable/rod connection the donor has; switch/door wiring connectors and ordinary slack; surrounding door flange, upper trim/window edge and interfering features relevant to access. No freestanding spring-loaded plate substitute.
exact_configuration.tool: Ordinary plastic panel-removal wedge/remover, expressly called for by page887. Exact production tool/SKU and blade/handle geometry remain to bind from a read source or actual sample; no fake long lever or large grip post.
exact_configuration.fixture: A rigid support may hold the genuine door shell at a documented ordinary service/open-door pose; it must not hold the trim, pre-release clips, delete the upper window hook/edge, or erase handle/wire interference. Full vehicle exterior unrelated to access need not be modeled. Fixture pose itself is a validity/access gate, not permission to shrink the door.
exact_configuration.end_support: An ordinary padded work surface/support for the detached trim is declared furniture, not a mechanism that completes disengagement. Its contact must genuinely support the real panel without relying on wiring/handle cable as a sling.

source_procedure_verified.provenance: Vehicle-specific CHARM workshop reproduction read through pinned third-party GitHub archive; it is not an independently authenticated Hyundai-hosted service-manual revision.
source_procedure_verified.page863: Door Trim Replacement first removes the quadrant inner cover, then loosens mounting screws and removes trim, removes the inside handle cage and disconnects connectors. Power Window Motor Replacement explicitly begins with front-door trim removal. The replacement procedure instructs checking connections/door function and replacing damaged clips; it does not supply clip dimensions or actuation forces.
source_procedure_verified.page887: Trim procedures specify a plastic panel-removal tool to avoid marring and caution against bending or scratching the trim/panels.

images_newly_viewed.945643715: Quadrant inner cover and real clip insert detail.
images_newly_viewed.945655092: Complete genuine front trim perimeter with multiple retaining sites; source is not a scaled coupon.
images_newly_viewed.945669489: Inside handle cage disengagement from the back of the trim; do not invent omission or a new Bowden-cable release method.
images_newly_viewed.945681280: Back-side electrical connectors that must be handled for complete separation. Exact donor connector count/options remain unbound.

normal_bounded_start.allowed: Quadrant cover and normal mounting screws already released/removed exactly as the real procedure allows; document whether each fastener is captive. Window/door state and work pose explicitly recorded. All targeted retaining clips are initially genuinely engaged; handle cage and all fitted electrical connectors remain in their real initial condition.
not_allowed: A clip already half-pulled through its hole
Hinged rigid panel replacing real clip-retained trim
Pre-disconnected plugs or removed handle cage while claiming complete trim-removal operation
A free panel that merely has to be transported
Removing essential surrounding door/window/handle geometry to grant fingertip access
normal_bounded_start.reason: This honestly bounds out prerequisite screw removal while preserving the physical retention/release skill. It is not a complete motor replacement. If scope is reduced to one clip, independently justify that the remaining operation is meaningful rather than borrow the whole service importance.

occupational_support.source_status: MIT-WAL pinned May2025 OEWS export mirror, not live BLS verification
occupational_support.task: Install, adjust, or repair hydraulic or electromagnetic automatic lift mechanisms used to raise and lower automobile windows, seats, and tops.
occupational_support.direct_bridge: The exact source makes trim removal a prerequisite to power-window motor repair, a named Core function. This is tighter than generic cosmetic/body-shop work. It does not show that a single isolated clip substep alone has the entire occupation’s importance.

actual_capability: Tool-mediated release of genuine clip retention while handling a large compliant trim section and its remaining attachments, followed by the real handle-cage and connector separation needed for service access. Difficulty must arise from access/contact and load-path preservation, not an invented order requirement.

comparison_to_1986.reference: Official PR1986 current inspected head, tasks/trim-clip/task.json; revision received/open.
comparison_to_1986.their_actual_scope: Align a loose splash shield hole to a body hole and push a loose rigid collar clip through both; their disclosed model moves sprung rods in the fixed hole instead of real clip barbs. The legitimate claim is aligning and fastening a flexible panel with a retaining fastener.
comparison_to_1986.our_actual_scope: Disengage initially retained trim by inserting a real plastic removal tool at the actual clip load path, support the panel as multiple real sites release, then preserve/unplug the back-side connections required for detachment.
comparison_to_1986.substantive_difference: Acquiring a leverage contact behind an engaged clip and controlling release/peel while supporting remaining attachments differs from holding holes aligned and pressing a loose clip in. The success conditions differ: released and intact assembly versus correctly fastened panel.
comparison_to_1986.strongest_duplicate_case: Same automotive plastic panel/clip setting and inverse retention action could still be treated as a component/task variant. Adding many identical clips or routine plugs is not alone a novelty justification. Do not use defects in their surrogate as a basis for claiming their active operation is unowned.
comparison_to_1986.gate: Before implementation, compare exact real clip engagement/release and central tool use against the earliest legitimate #1986 origin/scope and other accepted/pending trim-release tasks. If the difference reduces to reversing an ordinary clip insertion with no meaningful tool/panel constraint, PARK/REJECT rather than rename it.

other_comparators.lesson: Final rejection of a fake unlatched plunger and rigid spring-mounted panel; reinforces preserving real retaining interface. Its simulator-state expert objection is not valid under Version21.
Tool-assisted fuse extraction is a neighboring removal task; genuine trim-clip spring release, lever access and panel load path are the proposed distinctions, not simply a new object label.

implementation_approach_only.geometry: Derive real door flange/panel/clip-seat/upper-edge geometry from an actual matched assembly or traceable manufacturer CAD. Keep original scale, actual clip spacing and whatever edge-lift/unhook motion is needed. Reproduce only essential surrounding body features but all those relevant to the tool and wrists.
implementation_approach_only.mechanics: A reduced compliant panel model and local flexible clip/latch approximation may be disclosed under Version21 if real insertion/pry contacts generate release and the retained/open states follow actual geometric engagement. Calibrate to source/sample force-displacement and demonstrate partial/wrong contact negatives. Do not use tool proximity, elapsed time or preset trajectories to pop clips.
implementation_approach_only.handle_and_harness: Represent the actual handle-cage retaining tabs and all fitted plug latches. A bounded cable/harness representation may approximate material response, but it must retain real slack/interference and must not break, teleport, silently disconnect or magnetically park the panel. Do not invent a cable-release method not present on the actual donor.
implementation_approach_only.controller: A future expert may use simulator state for planning and operate real robot joints/tools; no teleporting parts or editing mechanism state. No controller or task code was written here.
implementation_approach_only.rendering_and_measurement: Visible clip-seat witness points/panel edges and appropriate camera views should permit the same released/retained checks on real hardware. Private geometry can aid scorer computation only when it maps to an independently observable physical criterion.

physical_scoring_proposal.full: Trim genuinely separated from all door clip/upper-edge/handle-cage and electrical attachments required by the chosen scope, intact and independently supported on the declared work surface, with all task-object load borne by genuine contacts and no dangling load on wires/cables. Door-side connectors/cable/handle mechanism and clip seats retain their expected condition. Both grippers may release once safe support is obtained; no arbitrary home pose.
physical_scoring_proposal.partial: Retained progress such as actual release of a documented subset of clip sites while the panel is safely supported, or all clips released with genuine handle/plug work remaining. Choose few physical milestones after measuring actual behavior; do not give permanent partial credit for a panel/seat destroyed to free it.
physical_scoring_proposal.zero_or_invalid: Remaining load-bearing clip/handle/plug connection when claiming complete removal, broken retention seats, wires pulled free rather than unlatched, severe new panel crease/marring, panel dropped or suspended by harness. Cosmetic failure threshold must use a reproducible photographed/straightedge baseline rather than vague pristine condition.
physical_scoring_proposal.simple_tools: Before/after photos with scale at identified clip/seat sites, straightedge/profile reference for permanent bending, inspection of real retainer tabs and connector bodies; independent light movement check that the detached panel is not still tethered. Do not claim a ruler can certify every hidden clip or cable; include views/inspection that expose the retained joints.
physical_scoring_proposal.not_yet_specified: No invented mm bend tolerance, pry-force threshold, panel mass, cable tension limit or clip count. Those depend on the actual donor and measurement protocol and are required before final scorer/implementation GO.
physical_scoring_proposal.clip_integrity_caveat: The reproduction says replace damaged clips; it does not establish that every clip is reusable. For the proposed non-destructive task, first demonstrate ordinary plastic-tool removal can preserve the selected retainers and all seats. If that is false, change the declared consumable/reset and scoring honestly or retire the intact-retainer scope; do not fabricate a reusable latch or silently reward destructive brute force.

cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.what: Record donor VIN/trim, panel/clip/tool part numbers, clip count/positions, handle-cage and plug variants, dimensions/mass, supplied state and ordinary work pose. Verify the source procedure applies.
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.stop: A generic body clip/plunger or enlarged trainer is required in place of genuine parts.

cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.what: Measure actual tool blade and handle, door flange, panel edge, clip recess, full panel dimensions, every clip release pose and final lift/unhook path. Transform finger/palm/wrist envelopes including opening/regrasp and the supporting arm. Check actual cable and handle-cage reach after panel pull-away.
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.stop: Any essential reach works only by shrinking/rotating the panel into an unsupported artificial posture, deleting real trim/window structure or enlarging the tool/tab. No native simulation needed.

cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.test: Benign real mechanism and force trace on available hardware
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.what: Hand-rehearse normal clip release with the ordinary plastic tool, measure force/displacement and repeatability, inspect clips/seats/panel afterwards. Include tool near-but-not-under-clip, a still-engaged clip, and excessive-offset pry controls. Demonstrate panel can be supported while handle cage/connectors are dealt with.
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.stop: A nearby wedge or generic upward pull always succeeds without the claimed release interface, genuine clip loads exceed practical grip/reaction, unavoidable damage occurs or no repeatable observable retained/released criterion exists.

cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.test: Paper/CPU mechanism sensitivity after separate implementation authorization
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.what: Only later, check candidate reduced panel/clip laws against measured release forces, partial engagement and wrong-contact states; source analysis/parameter fitting before native GPU.
cheap_disqualification_tests_ordered.stop: The only workable representation is prescribed clip release, a rigid spring plate or a hidden state transition disconnected from real contacts.

complexity_and_cost: Medium/high relative risk. This plan includes real panel compliance and multiple rear connections; it must not be advertised as a trivial rigid one-clip job. Its advantage is documented ordinary service and bounded localized material behavior, not low part count. No numeric cost or time estimate is evidenced.
biggest_missing_evidence: Actual compatible clip and panel geometry/part binding
Complete 1:1 stock tool/finger/palm access and full panel support path
Real clip release, panel flex, handle and connector forces
Origin-aware semantic novelty/ownership review against active #1986 and any current panel-removal tasks
go_no_go: GO for implementation planning/deep verification while these open requirements are explicit. Implementation itself remains NO-GO until exact parts/procedure applicability, genuine release/retention scoring and plausible real-scale stock-YAM access are bound and the active-neighbor comparison yields a meaningful distinct central operation.
